verdict.root_cause: At 22:22:36, five minutes before the 22:28:30 alert, platform-automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT on paymentservice to http://127.0.0.1:4317 [tr_6fa03767e678]. That value names an address where no collector listens, so paymentservice spans are exported into a black hole and its span-derived call metrics cannot be computed [tr_a34fb3d22c34], while the service itself keeps serving: charges are received and completed successfully through 22:30:16 with no error lines [tr_12485e04056c], and caller checkoutservice shows a flat-zero error ratio across the whole incident window [tr_c2d711c2f9d0]. The wrong endpoint value is the mechanism. The traces specialist's rule-out of this hypothesis does not hold: its window (04:28-10:28, samples 08:02-08:16) sits after the 06:40 revert and ~14h before the 22:22 re-application [tr_037f29f680c2], so it shows healthy export under the correct value, not the post-onset state. The identical edit applied and reverted ~16h earlier indicates an automation loop re-injecting it [tr_6fa03767e678].
verdict.reasoning: The request path is demonstrably intact: paymentservice logs are info-level charge successes to window close with no failing callee named [tr_12485e04056c], and checkoutservice's total error ratio is zero for 129 incident-window samples, which upper-bounds caller-side payment errors at zero [tr_c2d711c2f9d0]. What is absent is measurement, not health [tr_a34fb3d22c34]. The only onset-proximate change is the loopback OTLP endpoint [tr_6fa03767e678]; a loopback exporter target is wrong in itself and its wrongness is what breaks span delivery, so bad_config rather than bad_deploy (no release or image event recorded) or resource_exhaustion (no saturation data gathered). Fix is reverting the value and stopping the reconciliation loop that reapplies it.
open_questions: No post-22:22 trace query was run for paymentservice, so span absence after the re-application is inferred from the change record rather than observed.
What the 22:28:30 alert actually fired on is unknown; no latency, throughput, or saturation series was retrieved for either service.
paymentservice call metrics were empty in the two-hour baseline too, which may reflect a service_name label mismatch [tr_a34fb3d22c34] and would weaken metric silence as an onset signal.
The hostname change between log blocks [tr_12485e04056c] is undated - a pod replacement near onset is neither confirmed nor excluded.

alternatives.root_cause: No real service fault occurred; the alert is an artifact of a monitoring/label gap for paymentservice that predates the incident.
alternatives.why_not: The metric series is empty in both windows [tr_a34fb3d22c34], which supports a pre-existing gap, but it does not explain a change landing five minutes before onset [tr_6fa03767e678]; that coincidence is too tight to discard.

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice's ProductCatalogService/GetProduct hop is slow and dragged checkout latency, with paymentservice merely the alerting neighbour.
alternatives.why_not: The ~906-916ms GetProduct self-time was observed around 08:03-08:08 [tr_037f29f680c2], fourteen hours before onset, and no latency series was retrieved for the incident window [tr_c2d711c2f9d0].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring paymentservice's prior environment removes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317 (the recorded prior value for that key is unset, per the 06:40 revert entry in tr_6fa03767e678) and recreates the container. Observable within one recreate plus one export interval: a Tempo trace query for service=paymentservice over the post-action window returns traces again, each completed checkout trace containing a paymentservice `Charge` server span with its `charge` child, correctly parented under checkoutservice/hipstershop.PaymentService/Charge — the exact shape tr_037f29f680c2 recorded under the correct endpoint value. Secondary, weaker signal: calls_total{service_name="paymentservice"} may begin returning samples in Prometheus. Payment-path logs should be unchanged — charge-received / transaction-completed info lines resuming at their prior cadence after a short gap for the recreate (tr_12485e04056c).
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, 10 minutes after the recreate, a Tempo query for paymentservice over the post-action window still returns no spans (or checkout traces still show a gap where the Charge span belongs) — that would mean the loopback endpoint was not the reason spans are missing, or that spans were never actually missing post-22:22 and the alert fired on something else entirely. Also falsified in the other direction if paymentservice charge logs do NOT resume within ~60s of the recreate, or if checkoutservice's error ratio, currently flat zero (tr_c2d711c2f9d0), rises above zero and stays there. Note the honest gap: no post-22:22 trace query was ever run, so span absence is inferred from the change record, not observed. If the operator can run that query first, do that before acting — it costs nothing and converts this proposal from inference to measurement. Separately, if the config reappears within ~15 minutes (the automation reverted-then-reapplied this same key before), the revert has been overwritten by the platform-automation loop and the durable fix is upstream of this system.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this is a container recreate on a service that the logs show is currently healthy and completing charges through 22:30:16 — that is, it converts a telemetry-visibility defect into a real, if brief, payment outage for no gain. In-flight charge RPCs at the moment of recreate are dropped; paymentservice holds cache-only state so nothing durable is lost, but a customer checkout in flight can fail. Because the 22:28:30 alert's actual trigger is unknown and no latency, throughput, or saturation series was ever retrieved, there may be a second, unaddressed fault that this action neither fixes nor reveals — and the recreate will muddy timelines for whoever investigates it next. Reverting the endpoint also moves span export traffic back onto the real collector; if that collector is itself unhealthy, this restores load to it.
proposal.blast_radius: One service directly: paymentservice. checkoutservice is its named caller and will see connection resets or failed Charge RPCs for the duration of the recreate; frontend sits behind checkoutservice and will see those as failed or slow PlaceOrder calls, so the blast radius reaches end-user checkout for seconds to tens of seconds. Because the reverted value is a dependency address, the OTLP collector previously named by the correct endpoint will see paymentservice span traffic return. The action is reversible.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on paymentservice, a payment-path service with downstream checkout and frontend exposure, is not something to dismiss without evidence. Nothing in the alert pattern points to a specific fault class yet.
